data.description:
# S1 — One provider factory behind pydantic-ai's `infer_model(provider_factory=…)`

## Context / Problem

Provider construction is an inline special case. `src/rebar/llm/runner.py:268` reads
`if self._model_override is None and resolved.startswith("anthropic"):` and builds the retrying Anthropic
client in the middle of `run()`. Any second provider (Bedrock, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) has to add
another branch in the same place, which is how PR #121 was written. There is no single place that answers
"how is a Provider constructed for provider X".

## Approach

Introduce `src/rebar/llm/providers.py`: a small registry mapping a pydantic-ai provider name to a builder
`Callable[[str, LLMConfig], Model]`, exposed as one `provider_factory` suitable for pydantic-ai's
`infer_model(model_str, provider_factory=…)` hook. Upstream directs user-configurable-provider apps to exactly
this hook (pydantic-ai#1343) rather than patching `infer_provider`, so rebar depends on a supported contract
instead of a private one. The existing Anthropic construction moves verbatim from `runner.py:268` into an
`anthropic` builder that continues to call `_build_retrying_anthropic_model` in
`src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py`, keeping the tenacity transport, `max_retries=0` guard, loopback-proxy
bypass (`anthropic_model.py:60`) and per-request `httpx.Timeout` unchanged. `_pai_model`
(`anthropic_model.py:159`) remains the model-string resolver and is not touched.

This story is a **pure relocation with no behavior change** — it lands the seam before any new provider uses
it, so the Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible stories are additive registrations rather than surgery on `run()`.

**Alternative rejected:** a chain of `elif` branches in `run()` (PR #121's shape). It keeps provider knowledge
smeared across the runner, makes each new provider a diff to the hottest function in the module, and leaves
no place to attach capability lookups in S2.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` (new) — registry, `provider_factory`, the `anthropic` builder entry.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — replace the `:268` branch with a factory call; keep `_http_client` teardown.
- `src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py` — unchanged behavior; imported by the new builder.
- `tests/unit/test_llm_provider_factory.py` (new).

## Testing

Contract test tier (producer/consumer through the real seam): the factory is the producer and `run()` the
consumer, so a unit test on the registry alone is insufficient — the assertion must be that `run()` obtains its
model through the factory.

- happy path: with `REBAR_LLM_MODEL=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8`, the model `run()` builds is an `AnthropicModel`
  whose httpx client carries an `AsyncTenacityTransport` and whose `AsyncAnthropic.max_retries == 0` — the same
  assertions `tests/unit/test_pydantic_ai_runner.py` already makes, now routed through the factory.
- failure path: an unregistered provider name raises a `LLMConfigError` that names the registered providers,
  not a `KeyError`.
- negative control: the `model_override` test path still bypasses the factory entirely and builds no client.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `grep -n 'startswith("anthropic")' src/rebar/llm/runner.py` returns nothing
- [ ] the full existing suite passes unchanged (`make test`), evidencing no behavior change
- [ ] a new test asserts `run()` sources its model from `providers.provider_factory` and that an unknown
      provider raises `LLMConfigError` listing registered names
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` is under 300 LOC and imports nothing from `runner` (leaf module, matching
      the `anthropic_model.py` convention)
data.title: S1 — one provider factory behind pydantic-ai infer_model(provider_factory=…)
